functions.documentation: Build a canonical result for a product discovered without a CAOM sidecar.
functions.name: init

functions.documentation:
Returns true when this product contains any of the requested filter bands.

COAM `filters` values can be compound strings such as `"F444W;F405N"`.
Matching is case-insensitive and token based, so `"F150W"` matches
`"F150W;CLEAR"` but not `"F150W2"`.
functions.name: matchesObservationFilterBands

functions.documentation: Returns all valid values with descriptions for a categorical keyword.
functions.name: categoricalOptions

functions.documentation:
Returns the header keyword category for a given FITS keyword.

Covers both general FITS structural, scaling, WCS, and time keywords as well as
JWST-specific keywords from the MAST Instrument Keyword Dictionary at
https://mast.stsci.edu/api/v0/_jwst_inst_keywd.html
Returns `.unknown` for keywords not in the category map.
functions.name: category

functions.documentation:
Returns the human-readable description for a FITS keyword.
Falls back to a generic message for unknown keywords.
functions.name: description

functions.documentation: Returns whether the keyword has a well-known set of categorical values.
functions.name: isCategorical

functions.documentation: Returns the description of a specific value for a categorical keyword.
functions.name: valueDescription

functions.documentation:
Parse a semicolon-separated filter string (as returned in COAM results) into an array of ``JWSTFilter``.

Unrecognized filter names are silently skipped.

- Parameter filterString: A string such as `"F560W;F1000W"` or a single filter name.
- Returns: An array of matched ``JWSTFilter`` values.
functions.name: parseFilters

functions.documentation:
Look up a header by keyword name.
- Parameter keyword: The FITS keyword (e.g. "BITPIX", "TELESCOP")
- Returns: The first matching header unit, or nil
functions.name: header

functions.documentation:
Look up all headers matching a keyword.
Useful for keywords that can appear multiple times (COMMENT, HISTORY).
functions.name: headers

functions.documentation:
Cache MAST products and return their canonical CAOM records enriched
with the local files and metadata created by the download pipeline.

Both MAST URI products and direct HTTP products are supported. Existing
cache entries are reused by the underlying download methods.
functions.name: cacheDataProducts

functions.documentation: Remove all log subscribers
functions.name: clearLogSubscribers

functions.documentation:
Delete locally cached MAST products saved under SwiftMAST's `MAST` folder.

Pass a target name to delete only that target's local cache. Omit
`targetName` to delete the entire local MAST cache folder. This also
clears matching in-memory target assets and FITS metadata.
functions.name: deleteCachedMASTData

functions.documentation: Stop appending log entries to a file. In-memory logs and subscribers remain active.
functions.name: disableFileLogging

functions.documentation:
Attach locally cached files and metadata to remote or previously stored
products while preserving their original CAOM fields.

Results are matched using ``CoamResult/productIdentifier``. Products that
have not been cached are returned unchanged, which makes this suitable for
progressively enriching a query result as downloads complete.
functions.name: enrichWithLocalCache

functions.documentation:
Extract raw image HDU planes from a local FITS file without rendering them to JPEG.

This is the FITS-aware entry point used by astronomy image pipelines. It preserves
raw scaled pixel values, merged headers, HDU roles, and WCS metadata so the app can
perform histogram stretching, weight masking, color blending, and WCS placement.
functions.name: extractFITSObservationProduct

functions.documentation:
Fetch and parse remote FITS headers using HTTP byte-range requests.

This avoids downloading large FITS payloads. The parser reads FITS 80-byte
header cards and computes HDU data offsets from structural keywords, so it
can return image dimensions and WCS metadata even when image bytes are absent.
functions.name: fetchFITSHeaderSummary

functions.documentation: Fetch and parse remote FITS headers using HTTP byte-range requests.
functions.name: fetchFITSHeaderSummary

functions.documentation:
Fetch key image metadata from a ``CoamResult`` data URL without downloading
the FITS image payload.
functions.name: fetchPreferredFITSImageHeaderMetadata

functions.documentation:
Fetch key image metadata from a ``CoamResult`` data URL, preferring an
already-downloaded FITS file in SwiftMAST's local product storage.
functions.name: fetchPreferredFITSImageHeaderMetadata

functions.documentation:
Fetch only enough remote FITS bytes to identify the preferred image HDU and
return its key image metadata.

The request uses HTTP byte ranges and skips image payloads by computing HDU
data sizes from FITS structural keywords. The returned metadata describes
the primary image if the primary HDU contains image data, otherwise the
preferred science image extension when available.
functions.name: fetchPreferredFITSImageHeaderMetadata

functions.documentation:
Fetch only enough remote FITS bytes to identify the preferred image HDU and
return its key image metadata.
functions.name: fetchPreferredFITSImageHeaderMetadata

functions.documentation:
Reconstruct local cache contents using the same observation-group model
returned by remote MAST searches.
functions.name: getCachedObservationGroups

functions.documentation:
Return every product discovered in the local MAST cache as a canonical
``CoamResult`` enriched with its local files and FITS metadata.

Products without a `coam-result.json` sidecar are reconstructed from the
cache layout and available FITS metadata.
functions.name: getLocalCoamResults

functions.documentation:
Reconstruct observation groups from products available in SwiftMAST's local cache.

The scanner reads the standard product cache layout:
`MAST/<target>/<mission>/<observation>/<filter>/fit|image|preview`.
It attaches sidecar JSON when available, including `coam-result.json`,
raw/structured FITS metadata, preferred image metadata, and normalized WCS data.
functions.name: getLocalObservationGroups

- Parameter id: The subscriber ID to remove

functions.documentation:
Compare two JWST filter names by wavelength (ascending).
Filters with the same wavelength are further sorted alphabetically.
functions.name: compareJWSTFilters

functions.documentation:
Compare two filter names by wavelength (ascending).
Filters with the same wavelength are further sorted alphabetically.
functions.name: compareObservationFilters

functions.documentation:
Compare two products according to the given ``ObservationProductSortOrder``.

- `.filter`: sort by filter wavelength ascending; tiebreak by effective time then filter name
- `.time`: sort by effective time ascending; tiebreak by filter wavelength then filter name
functions.name: compareObservationProducts

functions.documentation:
Extract the observation group key from an HST/HLA-style `obs_id`.

HST product IDs commonly include one or more filter tokens after the visit
and instrument pieces. This keeps the prefix before the first filter token:
`"hst_10775_62_wfc3_f606w"` → `"hst_10775_62_wfc3"`.
functions.name: hstObservationGroupKey

functions.documentation:
Returns the effective observation time for a product.

Priority:
1. `t_min` (exposure start time), if > 0
2. `t_max` (exposure end time), if > 0
3. `t_obs_release` (product release date)
functions.name: jwstEffectiveTime

functions.documentation:
Extract the numeric wavelength from a JWST filter name for sorting.

Examples:
- `"F200W"` → 200
- `"F1000W"` → 1000
- `"F150W2"` → 150
- `"F444W;F405N"` → 444 (uses first filter in compound name)
- `"CLEAR"` → `Int.max` (non-standard names sort last)
functions.name: jwstFilterWavelength

functions.documentation:
Extract the observation group key from a JWST `obs_id`.

The key is the first 3 underscore-delimited segments:
`"jw02666-o007_t004_miri_f1000w"` → `"jw02666-o007_t004_miri"`
functions.name: jwstObservationGroupKey

functions.documentation: Returns the effective observation time for a product.
functions.name: observationEffectiveTime
